Analytics Methodology & Technical Framework

The SupeRR Selector pressure analysis engine evaluates delivery-level performance against empirical expected-value baselines constructed from all qualifying IPL and T20I matches (2022 onward). Ratings standardize performance over expected outcomes and apply empirical Bayesian shrinkage toward zero with tiered sample thresholds.

1. Expected-Value Baselines (Task 4)

413 discrete game-state buckets across all 2022+ competition balls. Second innings is partitioned by balls remaining [1-6, 7-12, 13-24, 25-36, 37-60, 61-120], Required Run Rate (RRR) in 0.5 rpo intervals (capped at 16+), and wickets in hand [1-3, 4-6, 7-10]. First innings incorporates match phase and venue par tertiles (<165, 165-185, >185).

2. Pressure Definitions (Task 5)

Batters: 2nd innings deliveries with RRR ≥ 9.0 or death overs (overs 16-20 / balls rem ≤ 30) in either innings.
Bowlers: 2nd innings core chase band (RRR 8.0-12.0) and last-over component (balls rem 1-6). Balls in both count once exclusively in last-over.

3. Three Ranking Sets (Task 2)

Set 1 (RR Players): Filtered to players who appeared for Rajasthan Royals.
Set 2 (Next Season Eligible): Proxy pool of players who appeared in the most recent two seasons (2025 and 2026), including RR players.
Set 3 (All Players): Worldwide pool of all players in the dataset regardless of nationality.

4. Tiered Thresholds & Formulas (Task 3 & 6)

RR Players: Min 30 pressure balls (batters), 24 band balls (bowlers); shrinkage $k=30$ / $24$.
Non-RR Players: Min 60 pressure balls (batters), 48 band balls (bowlers); shrinkage $k=60$ / $48$.
Formulas: Batters: z(Runs Above/100) − z(Dismissal Penalty). Bowlers: z(Runs Saved) + z(Wicket Comp) + 0.5 × z(Last Over Comp).
